_note: 第三種集型的事實庫:**同一個宣稱、跨多個領域**。跟 famous(一篇對一篇)和 lineup(一個效應家族的多次重測)都不同 —— 這裡的數字不是效果量,是『這個因素解釋了多少變異』,分領域列出。2026-08-30 建立,每個數字都附 quote(它出自摘要的哪一句)。
_why_new_kind: 10,000 小時法則在 effect_scan 裡分數 24,311,是 22 個候選裡的第一名,而且是第二名的 2.3 倍。但它的頭條數字是**變異數百分比**,套不進 make_episode.thresholds() 的 d / r 兩軌。硬轉成 r=sqrt(R^2) 雖然數學上精確,螢幕上卻會出現一個觀眾去查論文查不到的數字(論文寫 26%,我印 0.51)。所以寧可多一種集型,不要多一個對不上的數字。
_missing_note: 缺的欄位一律留 null 並在 missing 裡點名,**不推估**。統合分析涵蓋幾篇研究、總共多少人,摘要裡沒有,四個來源(OpenAlex / Semantic Scholar / PubMed / Europe PMC)抓到的摘要都一樣。要用就得我自己讀原文,在那之前旁白不准提。

episodes.claim: how much you practise is what separates the best from everyone else

original.title: The role of deliberate practice in the acquisition of expert performance
original.cited_by_approx_note: 文案用的『超過 N 次』。無條件捨去到百位,所以一定是保守的下界。

test.title: Deliberate practice and performance in music, games, sports, education, and professions: a meta-analysis
test.missing_note: 涵蓋研究數與總人數不在摘要裡,四個來源都沒有。**旁白與畫面都不准提**,直到我讀過原文。
test.unit: percent of variance in performance explained by deliberate practice

domains.name: professions
domains.pct_note: 原文是『less than 1%』。存成 1 並標記為上界 —— 畫面與旁白都要唸『less than one percent』,不能唸成 1%。

test.quote: We found that deliberate practice explained 26% of the variance in performance for games, 21% for music, 18% for sports, 4% for education, and less than 1% for professions. [Macnamara, Hambrick & Oswald 2014, abstract]
test.verdict_quote: We conclude that deliberate practice is important, but not as important as has been argued. [same abstract]

episodes.hook: How much you practise is what separates the best from everyone else?
episodes.hook_short: Practice is what separates the best?
episodes.tone_manual_why: 作者自己的結論是『important, but not as important as has been argued』—— 那是『真的有、但比宣稱的小』,不是『不存在』。判 gone 會是**過度宣稱**,而且直接跟我引用的那句話矛盾。這個欄位必須手填:famous_tone 靠信賴區間分檔,這裡沒有信賴區間,讓它自己猜就是拿缺漏當斷言(bystander_effect 那次的錯法)。

episodes.claim: standing in a powerful pose for two minutes makes you more powerful

original.title: Power Posing: Brief Nonverbal Displays Affect Neuroendocrine Levels and Risk Tolerance
original.quote: That a person can, by assuming two simple 1-min poses, embody power and instantly become more powerful has real-world, actionable implications. [Carney, Cuddy & Yap 2010, abstract]
original.n_quote: Carney et al. found that power posing affected levels of hormones such as testosterone and cortisol, financial risk taking, and self-reported feelings of power in a sample of 42 participants [Ranehill et al. 2015, p.653]

test.kind: conceptual replication, experimenter blind to condition
test.title: Assessing the Robustness of Power Posing: No Effect on Hormones and Risk Tolerance in a Large Sample of Men and Women
test.power_quote: Our statistical power to detect an effect of the magnitude reported by Carney et al. was more than 95% [Ranehill et al. 2015, p.653]
test.extra_quote: Neither of the other two behavioral tasks yielded significant differences by condition. [Ranehill et al. 2015, p.654]
test.verdict_quote: Using a much larger sample size but similar procedures as Carney et al. did, we failed to confirm an effect of power posing on testosterone, cortisol, and financial risk taking. We did find that power posing affected self-reported feelings of power; however, this did not yield behavioral effects. [Ranehill et al. 2015, p.654]
test.missing_note: 這一集沒有缺漏欄位 —— 全文讀過,每個數字都附原句。
test._claim_note: 四項都是同一個宣稱的不同量法,所以「4 個裡回來 1 個」是對的說法。

episodes.hook: Standing in a powerful pose for two minutes makes you more powerful?
episodes.hook_short: Two minutes in a power pose?
episodes.tone_manual_why: 四個結果裡有一個顯著(felt power, p=.017)、三個不顯著。判 gone 是**過度宣稱** —— 有一個真的重現了,而且是原作者也量的那一個。判 held 也不對 —— 那個頻道賣點的三個生理與行為結果全都沒重現。這一集的重點就是**哪一個活下來**,所以定調必須是 shrunk_real 並在片裡講清楚是哪一個。

episodes.claim: you learn better when you are taught in your own learning style

original.title: Learning Styles: Concepts and Evidence
original.journal: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
original.claim_quote: They called this interaction the meshing hypothesis which states that an individual learns better when taught in a mode of instruction (for example listening versus reading) that aligns with their preferred learning style (auditory, visual, respectively). [Rogowsky et al. 2020, Introduction, describing Pashler et al. 2009]
original.note: 這不是一篇提出主張的原始研究,而是**指出這個主張沒有證據、並且訂出該怎麼測**的評論。所以片裡不能說「2009 年有人發現…」——它從頭到尾都在說沒有。
original.say_origin: This one does not come from a study that found it. In 2009 four researchers reviewed the whole literature and reported that almost nobody had run the experiment that could test it. So they wrote down exactly what that experiment would have to look like.

test.kind: experiment following the prescribed design, whole 5th grade
test.title: Providing Instruction Based on Students' Learning Style Preferences Does Not Improve Learning
test.n_quote: Eligible participants included the entire population of 5th graders (ages 10-11 years) enrolled in a public middle school in rural Pennsylvania (N = 136). The actual participants were those students present for three consecutive days during which the study occurred (n = 125; 64 females/61 males).

outcomes.name: taught in their style
outcomes.note: 這就是整個理論要成立的那一項
outcomes.quote: There was not a significant main effect of instruction (F(1, 32) = 1.15, p = 0.29), nor an instruction by learning styles interaction (F(1, 38) = 1.16; p = 0.29).

outcomes.name: listening beat reading
outcomes.quote: A significant main effect for instruction was found (F(1, 110) = 4.92; p = 0.03) with students performing better when listening (M = 36.0, SE = 0.9) than reading (M = 34.4, SE = 0.8). This corresponds to an effect size of eta 2 = 0.04, which is considered small.

outcomes.name: visual types, both tasks
outcomes.quote: There was a significant main effect of learning styles (auditory vs. visual; F (1, 32) = 12.92; p = 0.001) with an effect size of eta 2 = 0.29 ... These results indicate that visual learners were significantly better at both listening and reading comprehension, as compared to auditory learners.
outcomes.name_long: visual types scored higher at both

test.verdict_quote: Results failed to find a significant relationship between auditory or visual learning style preference and comprehension. Fifth graders with a visual learning style scored higher than those with an auditory learning style on listening and reading comprehension measures. As such, and counter to current educational beliefs and practices, teachers may actually be doing a disservice to students by using resources to determine their learning style and then tailoring the curriculum to match that learning style. [abstract]
test.missing_note: 全文(Europe PMC fullTextXML)自己讀過,每個數字都附原句。
test.say_test: In 2020 a team ran it, on the entire fifth grade of one American public school. 125 children. Every child was tested for listening and for reading, and then taught in one mode or the other.
test.say_punch: The thing the whole idea rests on - being taught in your own style - came back at p of zero point two nine. Nothing. But two other things did come back, and neither of them is the theory. Everybody did better listening than reading. And the children labelled visual scored higher at both - reading and listening. That effect was seven times the size of the one that was significant in the other direction.
test.say_verdict: So the label does not tell you how to teach someone. At most it tells you who tests better overall. The authors put it plainly: teachers may actually be doing a disservice to students by using resources to determine their learning style and then tailoring the curriculum to match it.
test._name_note: name 是**畫面上的顯示標籤**(我寫的),不是引文 —— 所以可以為了版面縮短。真正不能動的是 quote 與 stat。原本較長的說法留在 name_long。
test._claim_note: 只有第一項是**那個宣稱本身**(教學方式 × 學習風格的交互作用)。另外兩項是順帶量到的、而且都跟理論無關。所以標題不能寫「3 個裡回來 2 個」——那讀起來像理論部分成立,而真相是**要成立的那一個沒回來**。

episodes.hook: You learn better when you are taught in your own learning style?
episodes.hook_short: Taught in your own learning style?
episodes.tone_manual_why: 要測的那一項(教學方式 × 學習風格的交互作用)p = 0.29,不顯著 → gone。但**片裡必須講清楚有兩件事是顯著的**,而且它們都跟理論無關:所有人聽比讀好(p = 0.03, eta2 = 0.04),以及被歸類成視覺型的人**兩種都比較強**(p = 0.001, eta2 = 0.29 —— 比那個小效應大七倍)。只講「沒效」會漏掉這一集真正的發現:分類沒有告訴你怎麼教一個人,它只告訴你誰考得比較好。

_unit_note: 兩種單位:`pct`(變異數百分比,10,000 小時那集)與 `d`(Cohen's d,power posing 那集)。**單位不同,畫面就不同** —— d 沒辦法畫成「佔滿格的幾分之幾」,所以走清單而不是長條。硬用同一種畫法就會出現一個觀眾無法解讀的比例尺。
